content_sections.body: Read the model aloud twice: 'I travelled to Hue by train last Friday and arrived before lunch.' Underline the words that show the situation, time, or result. In this lesson, report a completed journey with key time and place details. Keep the language connected: do not give isolated words.
content_sections.title: Notice form and meaning (8 minutes)

content_sections.body: Partner A begins a realistic exchange about reporting a completed trip. Partner B asks for one missing detail. Swap roles and make one change to the time, place, reason, quantity, or next action. Check that the exchange achieves: Report a completed journey with key time and place details.
content_sections.title: Guided dialogue (8 minutes)

content_sections.body: Create a short message about reporting a completed trip without reading the model. Include a main event or plan and one precise detail. Speak it once slowly, then once at a natural pace. Listen for whether the key information is clear.
content_sections.title: Independent response (6 minutes)

objectives: Report a completed journey with key time and place details.

listening.answer: The listener should understand that it concerns reporting a completed trip.
constraints: Keep the transcript private before the learner answers the first question.
Use only the supplied transcript; do not require media.
listening.goal: Identify the situation and a useful detail in a short message about reporting a completed trip.
listening.instruction: Listen once to a short message about reporting a completed trip. Answer the question before the transcript is revealed, then listen again and check the key detail.
listening.question: What is the message mainly about?

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is supplied.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when learner audio is unavailable.
pronunciation.goal: Make the key information in reporting a completed trip easy to hear.
pronunciation.instruction: Say the model for reporting a completed trip in two thought groups. Mark the pause between ideas, then stress the word that gives the key action, time, quantity, reason, or request. Record a second attempt after listening to your first attempt.
pronunciation.target: Thought-group pause and key-word stress in a completed journey

constraints: Name the learner and tutor roles before the first turn.
Use at most three tutor turns and stop after the agreed next step.
speaking.goal: Complete a clear, practical exchange about reporting a completed trip.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay reporting a completed trip. Learner role: explain the situation and give one useful detail. Tutor role: be a helpful listener, ask one specific follow-up, and confirm the next step. Begin with a natural greeting and finish once both roles agree on the next action.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before giving feedback.
Give concise feedback only; do not replace the learner draft.
writing.goal: Write a connected, useful short message about reporting a completed trip.
writing.instruction: Write a 35–50 word message about reporting a completed trip. Include the main event or plan, one precise detail, and the next action or response. Submit your own draft before requesting feedback.
